season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is rehabbing the knee injury from the Week 15 loss to the Chargers and his camp workload is still being managed, while OC Eric Bieniemy has stepped away after a family emergency; KC's 10.5 win total carries market skepticism, so treat Mahomes and Rashee Rice as priced-for-best-case rather than safe.

A ten-team head coaching carousel resets fantasy value: Stefanski to Atlanta, Monken to Cleveland, John Harbaugh to the Giants, McCarthy to Pittsburgh, Kubiak to Las Vegas, Minter to Baltimore, Mike LaFleur to Arizona, Saleh to Tennessee, Hafley to Miami, and Joe Brady promoted in Buffalo, so last year's usage patterns are unreliable priors.

Mike McDaniel landed as Chargers OC under Jim Harbaugh, putting Omarion Hampton in a motion-heavy speed scheme with Justin Herbert, whose high-TD low-INT profile is premium at 6 points per passing TD, though PFF flags LAC's 9.5 win total as an under candidate on schedule.

Klint Kubiak named Kirk Cousins the Raiders' QB1 over No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza to open camp, which stabilizes the run-first plan around Ashton Jeanty and funnels targets to Brock Bowers, with a midseason QB switch the main variance risk.

San Francisco is in flux: Kyle Shanahan is recovering from a concussion suffered in a July 14 car crash and expected back for the Week 1 opener in Australia, George Kittle opened camp on PUP after a January Achilles tear, and new signings Mike Evans (3 years, 60.4M) and Christian Kirk (calf strain) reshape the target tree, making Brock Purdy's weekly TD output volatile early.

Tyreek Hill was released by Miami in February and reportedly still has no power in his left leg after the dislocated knee, and the Dolphins under Jeff Hafley carry a 3.5 win total against the second-hardest schedule, so De'Von Achane's yardage is the only Miami asset worth paying up for (verify).

Malik Nabers tore his right knee in Week 4 last season and had a spring follow-up procedure, and with John Harbaugh and Matt Nagy expected to lean run-heavy behind Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr., Nabers' early-round price outruns his TD equity in a non-PPR build.

Super Bowl champion Seattle returns a dominant defense and the Darnold-to-Kenneth Walker core but opens camp with Zach Charbonnet, Kenny McIntosh and Nick Emmanwori on PUP and a new play caller replacing Kubiak, while sharps like the over on their 10.5 win total.

Matthew Stafford led the NFL with 4,707 yards and 46 TDs at age 38 and the Rams drafted Ty Simpson 13th overall as the heir, so the league's highest win total (11.5) supports Puka Nacua while Stafford himself is a classic TD-regression fade.

Travis Hunter is fully cleared from the torn LCL that ended his rookie year and Jacksonville plans primarily cornerback with a WR rotation, capping his offensive snap count; meanwhile Travis Etienne's exit to New Orleans opens a clear early-down path for Bhayshul Tuten.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur imports McVay-tree play action but the league's worst projected win total (4.5 line, hardest schedule) and a QB room where Jacoby Brissett just got a raise to 15.5M make No. 3 overall rookie RB Jeremiyah Love the one clean TD-equity bet (QB pecking order verify).
Kevin Stefanski with OC Tommy Rees brings a wide-zone, RB-and-TE-first offense, boosting Bijan Robinson's case as the top overall non-PPR pick and reviving extended Kyle Pitts as a TD-dependent dart.

Defensive HC Jesse Minter with young OC Declan Doyle keeps Lamar Jackson's rushing floor intact, but the offense skews younger with Zay Flowers rising and age-based erosion risk on Derrick Henry's goal-line-dependent profile.

Joe Brady's internal promotion with Pete Carmichael Jr. as OC means continuity for Josh Allen's rushing-TD ceiling, the single safest asset in a 6-point-passing-TD format, while Dalton Kincaid's usage remains a question.

Dave Canales returns with Jonathon Brooks cleared after two ACL tears and praised in camp, muddying Chuba Hubbard's grip on goal-line work; rookie ED Nic Scourton's Day 1 ACL tear hurts the DST outlook.

Year 2 of Ben Johnson with Caleb Williams and roughly 150 vacated targets from the Moore and Zaccheaus departures sets up Luther Burden III, whose elite YAC profile fits non-PPR because he creates yardage and TDs, not just catches.

Joe Burrow is healthy and the offseason focus was fixing the defense, so the Burrow-to-Chase TD pipeline remains one of the league's best 6-point-passing-TD stacks despite a market-skeptical 10.5 win total.

New HC Todd Monken runs a real QB battle between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, and his Ravens-style scheme funnels work to Quinshon Judkins on the ground while Harold Fannin absorbs the departed David Njoku's TE targets.

Post-McCarthy Dallas faces the fourth-toughest schedule with a 9.5 win total, keeping Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb startable on TD equity but without last cycle's volume certainty (staff details verify).

Sean Payton lost OC Pete Carmichael to Buffalo and analysts widely flag Bo Nix for regression, so Denver's 9.5 win total leans on defense; treat the passing-game pieces as priced above their TD floor (verify).

Dan Campbell stays but new OC Drew Petzing's Arizona-style multi-TE run lean threatens Sam LaPorta's target share, and Brian Branch's December Achilles tear (unlikely back before December) dents the DST early.
Green Bay lost DC Jeff Hafley to Miami's HC job but returns Jordan Love and a young receiver room at a 9.5 win total, a stable mid-tier passing-TD environment without a dominant target hog (verify).

C.J. Stroud gets a rebuilt line and traded-for David Montgomery to fix third downs (verify), while Christian Kirk's exit and Tank Dell's rehab make Jayden Higgins the yardage-and-TD riser next to injury-prone Nico Collins.

Daniel Jones is cleared from his torn Achilles and participating in camp, which restores play-action value for Michael Pittman Jr. and keeps Jonathan Taylor's goal-line role the offense's anchor at a modest 7.5 win total.

Liam Coen's offense replaces Travis Etienne with Bhayshul Tuten, whose 31 percent missed-tackle rate and TD burst fit non-PPR perfectly, while Travis Hunter plays primarily corner with only rotational WR snaps.

Mahomes' knee rehab and Eric Bieniemy's leave of absence cloud the operation, and PFF projects under their 10.5 line, so Chiefs pass catchers led by Rashee Rice carry more downside than their price implies.

Klint Kubiak's outside-zone scheme with Cousins named QB1 over No. 1 pick Mendoza is built to feature Ashton Jeanty's volume and Brock Bowers' target monopoly, the two assets that survive a 5.5-win team context.

Mike McDaniel as OC under Jim Harbaugh puts Omarion Hampton in a speed-and-motion workhorse role and keeps Herbert's high-TD low-INT profile premium, though the seventh-toughest schedule makes the team under the sharp side.

McVay's Rams own the league's highest win total (11.5) with a top-three easiest schedule, supporting Puka Nacua's yardage dominance, but 38-year-old Stafford's 46-TD season with heir Ty Simpson drafted 13th screams TD regression.

New HC Jeff Hafley with OC Bobby Slowik inherits a teardown with a 3.5 win total and the second-hardest schedule after Tyreek Hill's February release, leaving De'Von Achane's explosive yardage as the roster's lone premium fantasy asset.

Kevin O'Connell's continuity means Justin Jefferson remains a yardage-share monster regardless of QB growth, with Minnesota's 8.5 win total signaling a middling but pass-willing environment (QB depth chart verify).

The Super Bowl LX runner-up returns Drake Maye with a 10.5 win total, and the backfield behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson plus Harold Landry on PUP are the camp watch items; Maye skeptics note pricing has caught up to the breakout.

Tyler Shough closed his rookie year with six straight 17-plus-point games and second-most carries inside the 10 among QBs, and adding Travis Etienne and rookie Jordyn Tyson gives the Saints sneaky TD-scoring infrastructure at a 7.5 win total.

John Harbaugh with OC Matt Nagy will play field-position, run-first football, boosting Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr. TD equity while Jaxson Dart manages and Malik Nabers' surgically repaired knee makes his early-round price shaky.

Aaron Glenn kept his job and hired Frank Reich as OC, but the starting QB remains unsettled after the Fields benching, capping Garrett Wilson at yardage-only value on a 5.5-win roster until the job clarifies (verify).

Sirianni promoted Sean Mannion to OC amid declining Jalen Hurts red-zone rushing TDs, so Saquon Barkley's goal-line share could actually grow, keeping him elite in a non-PPR format even at a heavy workload age.

Mike McCarthy takes over with DK Metcalf as the clear X and Jaylen Warren positioned for a true three-down role, but the QB plan is publicly unresolved with ownership seeking clarity on the Rodgers question this month (verify).

Shanahan returns from his car-crash concussion by the Australia opener, Kittle starts camp on PUP post-Achilles, and Mike Evans (age 33) plus Christian Kirk (calf) join a 10.5-win roster where Purdy is undervalued and McCaffrey's 450-touch season is the workload red flag.

The defending champs under Mike Macdonald break in a new play caller after Kubiak left, with Darnold and Super Bowl star Kenneth Walker back but Charbonnet, McIntosh and Emmanwori on PUP; the 10.5 over is a popular sharp position and rookie Jadarian Price is the handcuff to know.

Todd Bowles imported Zac Robinson from Atlanta as OC, and with Mike Evans in San Francisco and Rachaad White gone, Emeka Egbuka steps into the alpha target role and Kenny Gainwell (13.3 touches, 17.8 ppg from Week 8 on) quietly claims backfield value.

Robert Saleh hired Brian Daboll to run the offense around Year 2 Cam Ward, with rookie Carnell Tate billed as the class's most pro-ready route runner giving Ward a real X receiver, though JC Latham's PUP stint threatens the protection plan.

Dan Quinn promoted David Blough to OC and the market gives Washington a favorite's 7.5 line against a soft schedule, but analysts flag Jayden Daniels' efficiency sustainability, making his rushing floor the reason he still prices as a top-five QB here.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Healthy ankle plus Mike McDaniel's new Chargers scheme that manufactured RB5-level seasons; a 20-plus-touch yardage-and-TD role is exactly what non-PPR pays for.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: No. 3 overall pick with elite speed and a three-down skill set; the last nine RBs drafted top-12 all finished top-12 as rookies, and Arizona has nothing to keep him off the field.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: Roughly 150 vacated Bears targets and a 2.92 yards-per-route-run rookie profile in Ben Johnson's offense; he scores on yardage and TDs, not catch volume, so his non-PPR gap to market is wide.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' exit hands him the Tampa alpha role after a 938-yard, 6-TD rookie year with four 20-point games; Mayfield's aggressiveness feeds end-zone targets.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Christian Kirk gone and Tank Dell rehabbing leaves Higgins as Houston's No. 2; big-bodied downfield role next to injury-prone Collins is a TD-equity play, not a slot-compiler trap.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Etienne's departure clears the Jacksonville backfield; 7 TDs on 93 rookie touches and a 31 percent missed-tackle-forced rate point to a high-end non-PPR RB2 path.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Kubiak's outside-zone scheme historically feeds one back 15-plus PPG, and Cousins starting stabilizes game scripts; Jeanty's 31.8-point ceiling game showed the talent.

breakout_watch.name: Brock Bowers
breakout_watch.why: Kubiak funnels Jaxon Smith-Njigba-style target volume to his chain-mover, and Bowers is the only proven pass catcher in Vegas; positional TD edge at TE.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Six straight 17-plus-point games to close 2025 plus second-most QB carries inside the 10; new weapons Etienne and Jordyn Tyson raise the TD ceiling in a 6-point-passing-TD league.

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: Todd Monken's Baltimore-style run game arrives in Cleveland and Judkins is the hammer; goal-line monopoly on a run-heavy team is gold in this format.

breakout_watch.name: Zay Flowers
breakout_watch.why: New Ravens staff is expected to modernize the dropback game around him; a yardage-per-target spike with Lamar's deep ball beats any catch-count concern here.

breakout_watch.name: Jaylen Warren
breakout_watch.why: Mike McCarthy has a long history of feeding one back, and Warren enters camp positioned for a true three-down workhorse role in Pittsburgh.

breakout_watch.name: Kenny Gainwell
breakout_watch.why: Averaged 13.3 touches and 17.8 points from Week 8 on and Rachaad White departed; a cheap Tampa backfield role with TD access (verify camp usage).

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: Seattle rookie who averaged 6.0 YPC in college lands behind a Super Bowl line with Charbonnet and McIntosh both opening camp on PUP; immediate No. 2 role with league-winning contingency value.

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Age-38 season after a career-high 46 TDs with heir Ty Simpson drafted 13th; TD regression plus benching-for-the-future risk makes his QB-high price the wrong side.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Coming off roughly 450 combined touches; the post-mega-workload season has repeatedly broken elite backs, and SF's crowded new target tree dilutes his TD share.

fade_watch.name: Derrick Henry
fade_watch.why: Age cliff plus a new defense-first Ravens staff that may spread the load; his value is purely goal-line dependent and the yardage efficiency is eroding.

fade_watch.name: Mike Evans
fade_watch.why: Age-33 debut season in San Francisco after missing 9 games with a career-low 12.1 PPG; only two 33-plus WRs in a decade have finished top-25, and Kittle plus Kirk compete for red-zone looks.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: Week 4 knee reconstruction plus a spring follow-up procedure, landing in a Harbaugh-Nagy run-first offense with a game-manager QB; early-round price, mid-round TD equity.

fade_watch.name: Rashee Rice
fade_watch.why: Short-area catch-volume profile is the worst archetype in non-PPR, and Mahomes' knee rehab plus KC's OC turmoil pressure the whole pass game's TD output.

fade_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
fade_watch.why: Njoku's departure has inflated his price past his outlier 2025, he logged suspiciously little offseason practice time, and defenses will scheme for him.

fade_watch.name: Sam LaPorta
fade_watch.why: New Lions OC Drew Petzing's multi-TE, run-lean scheme projects a target-share drop; paying a top-TE price for declining looks is the definition of a fade.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Age 28 with 2,100-plus career touches, YPC down to 4.0, and a knee-marred late-2025 fade from 19.6 to 11.3 PPG; the workload cliff profile (team situation verify).

fade_watch.name: Bo Nix
fade_watch.why: Widely flagged regression candidate after Denver lost OC Pete Carmichael; without elite rushing volume his 6-point-TD ceiling depends on efficiency he has not sustained.

uncertainty_note: It is the first week of full-squad camps (all 32 teams reported by July 28) and several value-defining questions are open: the Steelers and Jets starting QB jobs are unresolved, Arizona's QB hierarchy after Brissett's raise is unclear, Mahomes' practice workload and Bieniemy's timetable in KC are unknown, the Watson-Sanders battle in Cleveland is live, Seattle's play caller and PUP backfield timelines are unsettled, and PUP-list players (Kittle, Charbonnet, Branch, Landry, Latham) have no firm return dates; re-check all of these before drafting.
